The attack failed. I reproduced the verifier's read independently and found the passage word for word where the citation says it is.

THE TEXT. I downloaded the same scan the verifier names, archive.org journal-of-a-solitude-2014-may-sarton, 298,090 bytes of OCR, and searched it. The phrase 'Imitate the trees' is at byte 35,680, inside the entry headed October 6th. Here is the paragraph as the file has it: 'Does anything in nature despair except man? An animal with a foot caught in a trap does not seem to despair. It is too busy trying to survive. It is all closed in, to a kind of still, intense waiting. Is this a key? Keep busy with survival. Imitate the trees. Learn to lose in order to recover, and remember that nothing stays the same for long, not even pain, psychic pain. Sit it out. Let it all pass. Let it go.' The proposed quotation is those two sentences, exact, including the comma before 'and remember' and the appositive 'not even pain, psychic pain'. Nothing is elided, nothing is joined, nothing is minted.

THE LOCATOR. The entry head printed immediately above is 'October 6th', and the next head down the file is 'October 8th' (OCR'd as 'October Sth'). The entry opens 'A DAY when I am expecting someone for lunch is quite unlike ordinary days', and runs through Anne Woodson's visit, the ash tree letting fall the riches of a season, the two lines of Eliot, Mahler's Der Abschied, and then the despair paragraph. The verifier's description of the surrounding text matches the page, which tells me they actually read it. The journal runs from September 1970 to September 1971, one autumn only, so there is no second October 6th to confuse. A dated entry is an acceptable locator under rule 4, and it is a better one than a page number here, because Journal of a Solitude has been reset many times and the dated heads are stable across every setting.

THE PAGE NUMBER THE VERIFIER DROPPED. Dropping p. 34 was right and I would have dropped it too. The scan searched is a later reissue whose pagination cannot settle the 1973 Norton first edition, and a page number nobody has seen is precisely the confident false citation the standard forbids. The source line as it now stands claims only what has been read.

EVERY OTHER GATE. shipped.js: shipped [], near [], may sarton 0 of 3, not banned. Attribution is not in dispute and Sarton is on no trap in the misattribution list. No speaker to name: Sarton in her own journal. Scope: Journal of a Solitude, W. W. Norton, 1973, well before 1999, and not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. Publishable: the line names psychic pain and the paragraph before it names an animal in a trap, but the quotation stops short of that image and carries none of it; what ships is counsel, not description, and needs no warning. Theme fit for Impermanence is close to perfect and it is the one of the four that most obviously helps at six in the morning: nothing stays the same for long, not even pain. Prose, correctly not broken into lines. Source line is 81 characters, leads with the author's name, no dash, and runs work, then locator, then publisher and year in parentheses. Tag Diary is the form of the work, a dated journal. The quotation ends in a full stop and has no quotation marks or apostrophes to get straight.

ONE THING FOR THE EDITOR, NOT A REFUTATION. The note is accurate but its last clause, 'The copy searched is a later reissue, so its pagination does not settle the page of the 1973 first edition', lives in the evidence rather than the note, and the note itself already says the page could not be confirmed. That is fine. The only wording I would tighten is the edition field, 'Journal of a Solitude (W. W. Norton, 1973); text checked in a later reissue', which is honest and should be kept exactly as it is.
